certificate.description:
The certificate in PEM format.
The certificate chain must be no greater than 5 certs long.
The chain must include at least one intermediate cert.
certificate.rationale: This specifies the certificate to be used for SSL termination. The certificate is sensitive information and should be protected.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This controls the deletion behavior of the SSL certificate resource. It is important for managing the lifecycle of the resource and preventing accidental deletion.

description.description: An optional description of this resource.
description.rationale: This provides a description for the SSL certificate resource, which is useful for documentation and management purposes.

name.description:
Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is
created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with
RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and match
the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means the
first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last
character, which cannot be a dash.

These are in the same namespace as the managed SSL certificates.
name.rationale: This provides a unique name for the SSL certificate resource, which is useful for identification and management purposes.

name_prefix.description: Creates a unique name beginning with the specified prefix. Conflicts with name.
name_prefix.rationale: Used to only create a unique name for the SSL certificate resource, which is useful for identification and management purposes.

private_key.description: The write-only private key in PEM format.
private_key.rationale: The private key is highly sensitive information and must be protected to prevent unauthorized access to the SSL certificate.

private_key_wo.description: The write-only private key in PEM format.
private_key_wo.rationale: This is a write-only argument, and Terraform deliberately excludes write-only argument values from planned_values/state output. As a result, its content cannot be inspected by a plan-based OPA policy at all, so no generic platform security control can be enforced on it. Use of the write-only mechanism itself (over the plain private_key argument) is the security-positive choice, which is why private_key remains security_impact: true and is checked instead.

private_key_wo_version.description: Triggers update of 'private_key_wo' write-only. Increment this value when an update to 'private_key_wo' is needed. For more info see [updating write-only arguments](/docs/providers/google/guides/using_write_only_arguments.html#updating-write-only-arguments)
private_key_wo_version.rationale: Used only to trigger updates to the write-only private key. It does not directly affect security but is important for managing the lifecycle of the SSL certificate.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This specifies the project to which the SSL certificate belongs. It does not directly affect security but is important for resource management.
